title: footgun: ENTITY_ID_PATTERN plus the broken-reference machinery reads as a general 'detect references to missing blueprints' check.
detail: The pattern /\bentity_[a-z0-9]+\b/i only recognizes ids of the shape entity_<alnum>. Real blueprint/draftOption ids in src/data are nanoid-style (e.g. 0HNjKctJ5pN7Zwr6gV2ay) or human slugs (e.g. Accountant, 30_seconds_in) — 0 of 265 distinct ids are entity_-prefixed — so a missing reference to a real id never becomes a BrokenReference; broken detection fires only for the synthetic entity_ ids used in tests.

title: footgun: ENTITY_ID_PATTERN.test(value) reads as 'this string IS an entity id', so the recorded missingId is the referenced id.
detail: test() is a substring match anchored only by \b word boundaries, not ^...$, so any free-text string that merely contains an entity_ token (e.g. 'spawn entity_foo now') matches, and broken.push records missingId: value = the entire string, not the matched id. The later filter existingIds.has(b.missingId) then compares that whole sentence against the id set.

title: footgun: existingIds.has(value) paired with a case-insensitive ENTITY_ID_PATTERN suggests id resolution is case-tolerant.
detail: existingIds is a Set with exact case-sensitive lookup, while ENTITY_ID_PATTERN carries the i flag. A reference written as entity_A when the blueprint key is entity_a fails existingIds.has (miss), then matches the pattern, and is reported as a broken reference even though a case-variant of the target exists.

title: Broken-reference detection is inert on real ids: missing references never surface
detail: Because unresolved strings are only reported when they match the entity_ pattern, a payload/pool/blueprint that points at a real but non-existent target (nanoid or slug id) yields an empty broken list. Any consumer that trusts index.broken to catch dangling references gets a false all-clear on production module data.

title: filteredBroken filter is dead code and masks the real dedup intent
detail: broken.filter((b) => !existingIds.has(b.missingId)) can never remove an element: in walk.ts a value is pushed to broken only after existingIds.has(value) has already returned false, so every b.missingId is guaranteed absent from existingIds. The filter is a no-op that reads as a meaningful safety net; if the walk logic later changes to push existing ids, this line silently becomes load-bearing without any test exercising the removal.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: REAL: an unresolved string reference that does not match ENTITY_ID_PATTERN hits the bare `return` and is dropped with no incoming entry and no broken entry. Since real blueprint/draftOption ids are not entity_-prefixed, a dangling reference to a missing real id (e.g. a draft payload blueprintId or a pool optionId pointing at a deleted 'Accountant') fails completely untraced — the index looks healthy while the graph is broken.
